[`cvode()`](../reference/cvode.html) offers SUNDIALS CVODES [@hindmarsh2005sundials; @serban2005cvodes],
the long-established implementation of BDF and Adams methods with forward and adjoint sensitivities,
next to the integrators of `cppODE()`. It generates the model from the same equations and links it
against CVODES; the result is solved by `solveODE()`, `solveODEBatch()` and `prepareBatch()` as a
model from `cppODE()`. Forward sensitivities come from the CVODES sensitivity solver, reverse mode
from the CVODES adjoint, a continuous adjoint.

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Availability of SUNDIALS

`codegenAvailable("cvode")` reports whether the SUNDIALS libraries were found when cppDE was
installed.

```{r available}
codegenAvailable("cvode")
```

Without SUNDIALS ($\ge 6.0$) from the system, [`installLibs()`](../reference/installLibs.html)
downloads and builds SUNDIALS and SuiteSparse into a per-user cache;
`installLibs("suitesparse")` builds only KLU, the sparse linear solver of `sparse = TRUE` in
`cppODE()` and `cvode()`. cppDE records the library paths at install time, so it is installed again
afterwards ([Installation](installation.html)).

```{r installLibs, eval = FALSE}
installLibs("sundials")                       # SUNDIALS and SuiteSparse
remotes::install_github("dModverse/cppDE")    # links the new libraries
```

## Model definition

The arguments `events`, `rootfunc`, `fixed`, `forcings`, `sparse`, `includeTimeZero`, `stepTrace`,
`compile`, `modelname`, `outdir` and `verbose` are those of `cppODE()`. `method` is `"bdf"`
(default) or `"adams"`. Sensitivities are off by default: `deriv = TRUE` selects first-order
forward sensitivities, `derivMode = "reverse"` the CVODES adjoint with a checkpoint every
`asaCheckpoints` steps. There are no second-order sensitivities.

The native models for comparison:

```{r native}
eqns   <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms  <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)
times  <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)
events <- data.frame(var = "A", time = "t_e", value = "dose", method = "add")

chain  <- cppODE(eqns, modelname = "g8_chain", compile = FALSE)
dosed  <- cppODE(eqns, events = events, modelname = "g8_dosed", compile = FALSE)
chainR <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", modelname = "g8_chainR", compile = FALSE)
compile(chain, dosed, chainR, output = "guide8", cores = 2)
```

The same models on CVODES, compiled into a shared object of their own:

```{r cvode, eval = codegenAvailable("cvode")}
plainC <- cvode(eqns, modelname = "g8_plainC", compile = FALSE)
chainC <- cvode(eqns, deriv = TRUE, modelname = "g8_chainC", compile = FALSE)
dosedC <- cvode(eqns, events = events, deriv = TRUE, modelname = "g8_dosedC", compile = FALSE)
adjC   <- cvode(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", asaCheckpoints = 100, modelname = "g8_adjC",
                compile = FALSE)
compile(plainC, chainC, dosedC, adjC, output = "guide8cvode", cores = 2)
attr(chainC, "backend")
```

## Comparison with `cppODE()`

| | `cppODE()` | `cvode()` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `method` | `"bdf"`, `"adams"`, `"rb4"`, `"tsit5"` | `"bdf"`, `"adams"` |
| sensitivities | on by default; first and second order | `deriv = TRUE`; first order |
| reverse mode | discrete adjoint of the computed steps | continuous adjoint (CVODES) |
| reverse options | `keepStore`, `store`, `adjointControl()` | `asaCheckpoints`, `adjointControl(gradtol = )` |
| `sensErrCon` | `TRUE` or `FALSE` | `TRUE` |
| libraries | LAPACK; KLU optional | SUNDIALS; KLU optional |

Table: The two backends; details in [cvode() and the CVODES adjoint](methods-cvode.html#comparison).

At tight tolerances the two backends agree in states and sensitivities to the tolerance, with
different step sequences.

```{r compare, eval = codegenAvailable("cvode")}
solveODE(plainC, times, parms)$variable[101, ]

outC <- solveODE(chainC, times, parms, abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10)
outN <- solveODE(chain, times, parms, abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10)
c(states = max(abs(outC$variable - outN$variable)),
  sensitivities = max(abs(outC$tangent - outN$tangent)))
sapply(list(cvode = outC, cppODE = outN),
       function(o) unlist(o$diagnostics[c("accepted", "rejected", "fevals", "jevals")]))
```

## Events

Events, switches and forcings behave as in `cppODE()`; the sensitivities jump with the states,
also in the dose and in the event time.

```{r events, eval = codegenAvailable("cvode")}
pe   <- c(parms, t_e = 2, dose = 1)
outE <- solveODE(dosedC, times, pe, abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10)
rbind(cvode  = outE$tangent[101, "B", ],
      cppODE = solveODE(dosed, times, pe, abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10)$tangent[101, "B", ])
```

```{r events-plot, eval = codegenAvailable("cvode"), fig.height = 4.2}
ggplot(longFormat(outE, "A"), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

## Adjoint sensitivities

`derivMode = "reverse"` integrates the adjoint equations backward, one backward solve per cotangent
column, and interpolates the forward state between checkpoints. The result is the derivative of the
exact solution up to the tolerance; the reverse mode of `cppODE()` is the exact derivative of the
computed solution ([continuous and discrete adjoint](methods-cvode.html#asa)).
`adjointControl(gradtol = )` sets the tolerance of the quadrature of the gradient.

```{r adjoint, eval = codegenAvailable("cvode")}
w <- matrix(0, length(times), 2, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B")))
w[101, "B"] <- 1

cbind(cvode   = solveODE(adjC, times, parms, cotangent = w, abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10,
                         adjoint = adjointControl(gradtol = 1e-10))$cotangent[, 1],
      cppODE  = solveODE(chainR, times, parms, cotangent = w, abstol = 1e-10,
                         reltol = 1e-10)$cotangent[, 1],
      forward = outN$tangent[101, "B", ])
```

## Batches of conditions

A `cvode()` model has the batch entry of [6. Batches of conditions](guide-batches.html).

```{r batch, eval = codegenAvailable("cvode")}
conditions <- list(low  = list(parms = c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)),
                   high = list(parms = c(A = 2, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)))
batch <- solveODEBatch(chainC, conditions, times = times, cores = 2)
sapply(batch, function(r) r$tangent[101, "B", ])
```
